claims.text: Adding phosphorus to high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys improves glass-forming ability relative to otherwise comparable phosphorus-free alloys.
Adding phosphorus improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to otherwise comparable phosphorus-free alloys.
Phosphorus induces changes in alloy structure and properties.
Phosphorus changes the thermodynamic properties of the alloy.
Phosphorus changes the kinetic properties of the alloy.
The phosphorus-induced thermodynamic and kinetic changes lead to improved glass-forming ability.
The phosphorus-induced thermodynamic and kinetic changes lead to improved thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Whether phosphorus provides the predicted improvements depends on alloy composition.
Whether phosphorus provides the predicted improvements depends on cooling rate.
Whether phosphorus provides the predicted improvements depends on thermal-treatment conditions.
The exact mechanism by which phosphorus would improve glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability is not well understood.
